title: A comprehensive computer aided approach to design of earthen dams
author: Sobótka, Różański, et al.

steps.title: Reconstruct Terrain Surface and Soil Layers
steps.instruction: Create a 3D numerical model of the terrain and subsoil based on hypsometric maps and geotechnical investigation data (boreholes/soundings).

substeps.instruction: Define the analysis area, extending the domain by at least the total width of the dam in each direction to minimize boundary condition influence.
Generate a 3D terrain mesh model using CAD tools and transfer it to Finite Element (FE) software as the top boundary.
Set the lower boundary depth to be at least several times greater than the height of the dam.
Reconstruct geotechnical layers by assigning materials and parameters to each element using geostatistical interpolation (e.g., kriging).

Establish the semi-variogram function (typically spherical or exponential models) and determine the correlation length/radius via weighted least squares approximation or based on dam dimensions (e.g., 500 m).
Minimize the error variance of the interpolated variable using available borehole data.

steps.title: Evaluate Groundwater Flow and Cut-off Screen Depth
steps.instruction: Perform a parametric analysis of the 3D model to determine the cut-off screen depth and anchorage length to prevent internal erosion, soil boiling, and soil uplift.

substeps.instruction: Solve an initial-boundary value problem for transient flow in a partially saturated medium using the van Genuchten model for soil-water retention and Richards hypothesis for gas phase continuity.
Optionally divide the model into two parts to analyze each abutment separately to save resources.
Define boundary conditions (BCs): extrapolate the groundwater table to vertical planes on upstream/downstream sides as pore water pressure increasing linearly with depth (0 at water table).
Set remaining boundaries as impermeable and solve the steady-state problem to establish initial conditions for transient flow analysis.
Apply a time-varying hydrostatic water pressure BC to the reservoir basin based on anticipated damming levels, basin geometry, and stream discharge.
Calculate the hydraulic gradient (i) using Darcy's law: i = v/k, where v is fluid velocity and k is hydraulic conductivity.
Determine critical hydraulic gradients (icr) using the Abramov formula: icr = 0.032 * k^(-2/3), where k is in m/s.
Verify the limit state using the multiplicity of the limit admissible gradient: Fi = (γi * i) / icr. The condition is met if Fi ≤ 1.0 across the domain over all time steps.
Identify permeable layers (k > 1.0e-3 m/s or two orders of magnitude larger than the dominant layer at the cut-off wall base) and ensure the cut-off wall partitions these layers.
Adjust cut-off wall depth and anchorage length via parametric analysis if Fi > 1.0 or if permeable layers are not sufficiently partitioned.

steps.title: Assess Deformation and Stability
steps.instruction: Perform 2D stability and settlement analyses on selected plane cross-sections extracted from the 3D model using the Shear Strength Reduction (SSR) technique.

substeps.instruction: Extract 2D cross-sections based on dam size, soil layer arrangement, and terrain geometry.
Apply the Mohr-Coulomb elastic-plastic constitutive model for the subsoil and dam body.
Model the staged construction of the dam by sequentially adding layers (e.g., initial geometry, anti-filtration barrier execution, and completed construction).

Calculate settlements as the increment of vertical displacement at the foundation level between the reference state and completion; verify that the maximum displacement is within admissible legal/standard limits.
Perform stability analysis with hydromechanical coupling using effective strength parameters to verify general stability, soil boiling, and soil uplift.
Calculate the relative safety margin: F(t) = FOS / FOSmin, where FOS is the factor of safety and FOSmin is the minimum required value. The condition is met if F(t) ≥ 1.
Repeat stability analysis at least a dozen times for selected moments during the transient flood event to find the minimum FOS.
Evaluate all construction and operational phases; if limit states are not met, adjust dam shape, reinforce subsoil, or increase barrier depth and repeat Steps 2 and 3.
